checks.value: Executive Officers of the Registrant (As of March 11, 1994)

triage.note: Found by the T3-T5 cold review (G1 ledger row). segment.py's IBR test splits the item body at the first sentence terminator and asks whether THAT sentence matches IBR_RE -- then searches EXTERNAL_DOC_RE over the ENTIRE body rather than over the first sentence. So the rule the docstring describes ('the whole item is a pointer') is not the rule implemented ('the first sentence is a pointer, and the words "proxy statement" appear anywhere in the next 40,000 characters'). Pointer-sentence-first-then-inline-content is the majority modern layout for Item 10 (the proxy cross-reference, then the executive-officer table that Item 10 requires to be in the 10-K itself), and occurs again on Item 12 (proxy pointer, then the equity-compensation-plan table) and throughout Item 15 exhibit indexes. The consequence is severe and completely silent: validate.py builds its span map from status == 'extracted' only, so an item flipped to incorporated_by_reference escapes ALL SIX validators, and extract.py drops it from the extracted set before doc_status is derived, so the envelope stays clean. The eval adapter is equally blind -- no_overlap_ordered and verbatim both iterate the extracted list. Thousands of characters of real, correctly-located content get reported as living in another document, with zero warnings and confidence 0.85. This case is the reason the G1 batch also extends INV-S1 and boundary hygiene to cover IBR spans: fixing the sentence-order rule alone would close this instance while leaving the next misclassification just as silent.

provenance: SELF-CREATED adversarial fixture: a copy of evals/fixtures/ge-1994/filing.txt (General Electric Company FY1993 10-K -- see that fixture's README row for original public-source provenance), mutated 2026-08-16 by one documented, reproducible transformation. THE MUTATION IS A PURE REORDERING: the four-line paragraph at source lines 1372-1375 ('The remaining information called for by this item is incorporated by / reference to "Election of Directors" in the definitive proxy statement / relating to the registrant's Annual Meeting of Share Owners to be held / April 27, 1994.') was moved from the END of Item 10 to immediately AFTER the 'Item 10. Directors and Executive Officers of Registrant' heading line, ahead of the executive-officer table that follows it. Not one character of content is added, deleted or edited -- the derivation script asserts that the sorted multiset of all non-blank lines is IDENTICAL before and after, and that assertion is part of the reproduction recipe. This is not a straw man: the mutated order is the more common of the two real-world layouts, and GE's own Item 12 already uses pointer-first ordering elsewhere in the same document. MEASURED EFFECT (run 2026-08-16 against the T5 pipeline, before any fix): item 10 flips from 'extracted' with a 4,805-char span (the value the unmutated ge-1994-oldformat case asserts, with the stated reasoning 'the item has substantial extracted content beyond the pointer sentence') to 'incorporated_by_reference' with null chars, at confidence 0.85. Every other item is byte-identical in status and length to the unmutated run, doc_status stays 'success_with_warning', and the warning list is unchanged at ['unattributed_content'] -- nothing anywhere in the envelope registers that a 4,805-char section was disowned. WHY THESE CHECKS: item_present(10, extracted) is the direct assertion and fails today. Anchor counts verified by direct substring count on the mutated fixture's normalized text: 'Executive Officers of the Registrant (As of March 11, 1994)' occurs exactly 1x and 'Date assumed' exactly 1x -- both sit INSIDE the officer table, i.e. inside the content the bug disowns, so neither can be satisfied by a span that stops at the pointer paragraph, and both are unreachable from any other item. min_chars(10, 3000) sits below the true 4,805 and far above the 0 chars an IBR item reports, pinning the same thing numerically for the failure mode where the item is extracted but truncated to just the pointer sentence. items 7 and 11 are asserted as 'incorporated_by_reference' deliberately: they are genuine whole-item pointers in this filing and must NOT move, so the case proves the fix discriminates rather than simply disabling IBR classification -- a fix that turned every pointer into 'extracted' would go red here. expected_set_complete and only_items carry the same 14-item pre-1997 legacy set as ge-1994-oldformat; reordering two paragraphs cannot change a filing's item inventory. Tagged 'invariant' because the failure produces a confident, clean-looking envelope while silently dropping a whole section from the extracted set -- the exact silent-failure class the invariant suite exists to make non-negotiable, and the class the analysis report's silent-failure-rate metric is meant to measure.
